requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: A valid root cron entry schedules the exact command at 02:15 daily. Cronie is enabled and active, and cronnext independently calculated matching executions at 02:15 on two consecutive days. The configuration and service remained healthy after restart.

The cron command appends stdout and stderr to the required log. Direct executions appended output, the first entry survived restart, and a post-restart execution appended another entry. The persistent log has appropriate ownership, permissions, and SELinux context.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after implementation, node1 remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The solution uses the already-installed Cronie service, which successfully parsed and retained the configuration across restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged restart, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered system, Cronie, configuration, and retained log data. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No naturally timed 02:15 cron invocation was captured because the evidence window ended before the next scheduled execution. Scheduling is nevertheless strongly supported by the installed valid entry, active scheduler, calculated consecutive execution times, and direct command/output tests.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The cron file and log creation were required implementation changes (cmd-246f7bf82816434f); the two log appends were bounded behavior and persistence tests (cmd-db11a06278f84aa9, cmd-24333492cdee4a31); and the transient reboot timer was required by the provider restart protocol and did not remain afterward (cmd-9c0cdd6838b24f60, cmd-24333492cdee4a31). Final observations show no failed services, damaged package state, or new network exposure.
